name: Voting Rights Act of 1965
description: The Voting Rights Act of 1965, signed by President Lyndon B. Johnson on August 6, 1965, is the statute that finally enforced the Fifteenth Amendment across the Jim Crow South. Answering Selma directly — Johnson had asked Congress for the bill in his 'We Shall Overcome' address that March — the Act suspended literacy tests and other devices used to exclude Black voters, authorized federal examiners to register voters where local officials would not, and, in its Section 5 preclearance formula, required covered jurisdictions to prove to the federal government, in advance, that any change to their voting rules was not discriminatory. The effect was immediate and measurable: Black voter registration in Mississippi rose from 6.7 percent in 1964 to 59.8 percent by 1967. The Act was renewed and extended by Congress in 1970, 1975, 1982, and 2006; its preclearance formula was struck down by the Supreme Court in Shelby County v. Holder (2013), after which covered states moved quickly to change voting rules the formula would once have reviewed. With this record, the timeline's legislative triptych — 1964, 1965, 1968 — stands complete in the graph.

name: Vee-Jay Records
description: Vee-Jay Records was a pioneering Black-owned record label founded in 1953 in Gary, Indiana — not Chicago, as shorthand often has it — by husband-and-wife team Vivian Carter and James C. Bracken, who named it from their initials, V and J. Carter, a record-store owner who also worked as a Chicago disc jockey, built the label's business on blues, R&B, and gospel, later adding jazz; bluesman Jimmy Reed was signed while working in the Chicago stockyards. Carter's brother Calvin Carter ran A&R, and Ewart Abner joined in the mid-1950s, rising to president. Vee-Jay became the early American home of the Beatles and also recorded the Four Seasons and Jimmy Reed, with offices on Chicago's Record Row at 2129 S. Michigan Avenue. The success outran the business: Vee-Jay filed for bankruptcy in 1966 (the month is disputed across sources), with a reported debt of about $3 million. CTL's label research grades the Gary founding as consistent across encyclopedia, NPR, Smithsonian, and Indiana history sources.

name: Vivian G. Harsh
description: Vivian G. Harsh (1890–1960) was a Chicago librarian who built the landmark Black history collection that now bears her name. The graph record identifies her as Chicago's first Black librarian; CTL's preservation research specifies the documented first: on January 18, 1932, she became the first African American branch manager in the Chicago Public Library system, at the George Cleveland Hall Branch in Bronzeville. There she built the "Special Negro Collection" from 1932 — modeled on the Schomburg, Fisk, and Atlanta University collections — gathering books, photographs, clippings, and donations from Bronzeville patrons including Richard Wright and Langston Hughes, beginning with more than 100 books donated by NAACP founder George Bentley, because the library system provided no funding for it. The collection moved to the Carter G. Woodson Regional Library in 1975 and was renamed the Vivian G. Harsh Research Collection of Afro-American History and Literature; Chicago Public Library describes it as the largest Black history collection in the Midwest, and CTL's preservation findings grade it the oldest and largest in the Midwest.

name: Video Advertising Bureau (VAB)
description: The Video Advertising Bureau (VAB) is a trade advocacy group representing television networks, the sellers of television advertising. In research published during its dispute with Nielsen, the VAB asserted that Nielsen's errors left 30 billion advertising impressions uncounted, including 7 billion Black impressions and 5.5 billion Hispanic impressions, representing 350 million dollars in advertisements marketers could not buy. The study extrapolated from eight of sixteen months of Nielsen data. Nielsen disputed the VAB's methodology and maintained its data was directionally sound. The VAB also argued that Nielsen's numbers significantly undercounted Black, Hispanic, and younger audiences, especially during the pandemic, and petitioned the Media Rating Council to suspend Nielsen's accreditation. CTL records the bureau's figures as its reported advocacy position, not as independently verified measurement.

name: Vic Mensa
description: Vic Mensa is the performing name of Victor Kwesi Mensah (born June 6, 1993, in Chicago's Hyde Park), a rapper, singer, and activist formed by the same South Side ecosystem this graph documents street by street. A Whitney Young Magnet High School student, he helped form the band Kids These Days in 2009; the group released the Hard Times EP (2011) and the Traphouse Rock mixtape (2012) before splitting in May 2013. His solo debut mixtape Innanetape followed that September, and XXL named him to its 2014 Freshman Class. Roc Nation announced his signing in April 2015, days after 'U Mad,' his collaboration with Kanye West, appeared; as a co-writer of West's 'All Day' he was nominated for Best Rap Song at the 2016 Grammy Awards. His debut studio album, The Autobiography — executive produced by No I.D. and released July 28, 2017, on Roc Nation and Capitol — turned Hyde Park memory into literature. In 2018 he founded the SaveMoneySaveLife Foundation, funding health and arts programs in Chicago, including StreetMedics first-responder training. The audit found his graph record at sixteen words; this enrichment gives the hometown artist the full entry.

name: Vince Staples
description: Vince Staples (born Vincent Jamal Staples on July 2, 1993, in Compton, California) is an American rapper from the Ramona Park neighborhood of North Long Beach. He emerged through the Odd Future orbit and the 2013 mixtape Stolen Youth, produced by Mac Miller, signed with Def Jam, and broke through with the EP Hell Can Wait (2014) and his debut album Summertime '06 (2015), whose “Norf Norf” became a gold-certified signature. Big Fish Theory (2017) folded electronic and dance influences into his stark Long Beach storytelling, and FM! (2018), the self-titled Vince Staples (2021) and Ramona Park Broke My Heart (2022) followed; Dark Times (2024) closed his Def Jam tenure. AllMusic singles out his forward-thinking production choices and lyrical introspection as the marks of one of contemporary rap's most talented voices.

name: Voodoo
description: Voodoo is the second studio album by D’Angelo, released on January 25, 2000, on Virgin Records. Recorded during 1998 and 1999 at Electric Lady Studios in New York City with the Soulquarians collective — among them Questlove, James Poyser, and J Dilla — the album traded the structured songcraft of Brown Sugar (1995) for a loose, groove-first funk: rhythm sections playing behind the beat, layered vocals, and songs that unfold like studio jams. Its best-known track, “Untitled (How Does It Feel),” paired a Prince homage with a minimalist music video that made D’Angelo a mainstream figure and, by his own later account, a burdened one. Voodoo debuted at number one on the Billboard 200 with 320,000 first-week copies and won the Grammy Award for Best R&B Album; “Untitled” won Best Male R&B Vocal Performance. Rolling Stone ranked it number 28 on its 500 Greatest Albums of All Time, and critics regard it as a creative milestone of the neo-soul era.

name: Viola Desmond
aliases: Viola Irene Desmond; Viola Davis Desmond
description: Viola Desmond built a business before she made history. Trained as a beautician, the Halifax-born entrepreneur opened her own salon and founded the Desmond School of Beauty Culture, mentoring young Black women across Nova Scotia and the wider Maritimes at a time when Black women were largely shut out of professional training. On November 8, 1946, stranded in New Glasgow when her car broke down, she went to a film at the Roseland Theatre and took a main-floor seat after being sold a cheaper balcony ticket. Ordered to move to the section reserved for Black patrons, she refused. She was dragged out, jailed overnight, and convicted of tax evasion over the one-cent difference between the two seats — a charge that exposed the machinery of segregation in supposedly tolerant Canada. Her appeal failed, and the conviction stood in her lifetime, but her case galvanized Black Nova Scotian organizing and became one of Canada's most publicized confrontations with anti-Black discrimination. Desmond died in New York on February 7, 1965. Canada answered late: a posthumous free pardon in 2010, the first of its kind in the country, and in 2018 her portrait on the ten-dollar banknote, making her the first Canadian-born woman to appear alone on a Canadian bank note.

name: Victory Apostolic Church
aliases: Victory Apostolic Church of Matteson; VAC Matteson
description: Victory Apostolic Church is an Apostolic Pentecostal congregation founded by the Rev. Andrew D. Singleton Jr. Its first service was held on August 4, 1996, in Harvey, Illinois, where the young church met at a former Ramada Inn; a year later it moved to Chicago Heights, where it worshipped for twelve years and grew rapidly. In February 2009 Victory moved to its present home in Matteson, Illinois — a 12-acre campus with a 2,500-seat sanctuary, built at a reported cost of $20 million, the figures the church itself publishes. Singleton, who was mentored by Bishop Arthur M. Brazier of Chicago's Apostolic Church of God, remains senior pastor three decades on; the congregation marked its 30th anniversary in 2026. The church's published campus figures are carried here as attributed claims from its own materials, per GOV-004.

name: Vinícius Júnior
aliases: Vinícius José Paixão de Oliveira Júnior; Vini Jr.
description: Vinícius Júnior, born Vinícius José Paixão de Oliveira Júnior on 12 July 2000 in São Gonçalo, Brazil, is a Brazilian forward for Real Madrid and the Brazil national team, known for his pace, technique and dribbling. He debuted for Flamengo at 16 in 2017 and moved to Real Madrid in 2018, after his 18th birthday, in a deal reported as a national record for a player under 18. He scored the winning goal in the 2022 Champions League final and the second goal in the 2024 final, and was named the tournament's Player of the Season for 2023–24. In December 2024 he was named The Best FIFA Men's Player, finishing ahead of Rodri and Jude Bellingham, after helping Madrid to a La Liga–Champions League double; he was also runner-up in the 2024 Ballon d'Or voting. A Black Brazilian, he has been subjected to repeated racist abuse in Spanish football and has spoken out publicly against racism; the May 2023 abuse at Valencia's Mestalla led to the first criminal convictions for racism in Spanish professional football.

name: Victor Wembanyama
description: Victor Wembanyama, born 4 January 2004 in Le Chesnay, France, is a French professional basketball player for the San Antonio Spurs. The son of Felix Wembanyama, a track and field athlete of Congolese descent, and Elodie de Fautereau, a former basketball player and coach, he developed in France with Nanterre 92, ASVEL and Metropolitans 92, winning the French league's Most Valuable Player award in 2023. San Antonio selected him first overall in the 2023 NBA draft. He was the unanimous NBA Rookie of the Year in 2024, the first rookie named to the All-Defensive First Team, and he led France to a silver medal at the 2024 Paris Olympics. After a blood-clot diagnosis shortened his second season, he returned in 2025-26 to average career highs of 25.0 points and 11.5 rebounds, win Defensive Player of the Year as its youngest and first unanimous recipient, and carry San Antonio to the 2026 NBA Finals, where the Spurs fell to New York in five games. He signed a multi-year extension with San Antonio in July 2026.

description: Vladimir Guerrero Jr., born 16 March 1999 in Montreal, Canada, and raised largely in the Dominican Republic, is the Toronto Blue Jays' first baseman and the son of Hall of Famer Vladimir Guerrero Sr. Signed by Toronto in 2015, he debuted in 2019 and grew into the franchise's centerpiece, signing the largest contract in club history. His defining run came in October 2025, when he hit .442 with six home runs in the postseason, won the American League Championship Series MVP Award, and led Toronto to its first World Series since 1993. His 2026 season was, as reported, a difficult one — a .263 average with 9 home runs and 56 RBI in 142 games amid injuries — and on 25 September 2026 he publicly apologized to fans and teammates for comments made during the slump, on his father's counsel. CTL stages him as an Afro-Dominican ballplayer by documented paternal descent; the individual documentation gap is named below.

name: Vanessa Williams
aliases: Vanessa Lynn Williams; Vanessa L. Williams
description: Vanessa Williams is an American singer, actress, model and producer, born March 18, 1963. She gained recognition as the first Black woman to win the Miss America title, crowned Miss America 1984 on September 17, 1983. In July 1984, weeks before the end of her reign, she resigned after Penthouse magazine bought and published nude photographs of her without her consent, and first runner-up Suzette Charles succeeded her. Thirty-two years later, in September 2015, the Miss America organization publicly apologized to Williams when she returned as head judge for the Miss America 2016 pageant. Williams rebuilt her career in music and acting. She released her debut album The Right Stuff in 1988; its single Dreamin' peaked at number 8 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1989. Her second album, The Comfort Zone (1991), produced her signature number-one single Save the Best for Last. She earned multiple Grammy Award nominations, performed on Broadway, and in 2024 released Survivor, her ninth studio album and her first studio album in fifteen years, on her own Mellian Music label.

name: Very Smart Brothas
description: Very Smart Brothas is a Black American blog launched in 2008 by Damon Young and Panama Jackson. The two writers, fans of each other's work who connected online before ever meeting in person, built the site around humorous, conversational essays on pop culture, politics, dating, and relationships for a Black audience. By 2011 the blog averaged about 200,000 unique visitors a month, drew hundreds of comments per post, had published more than 750 posts, and had won two 2010 Black Weblog Awards, for Best Group Blog and Best Humor Blog. Young and Jackson also carried the brand into print with a self-published dating guide in 2011. In July 2017 Gizmodo Media Group acquired the blog, and Very Smart Brothas became a vertical of The Root, where Jackson is identified in the later coverage as a senior editor. The lineage matters because the site began as an independent two-person operation and ended the decade inside a larger Black media platform.

name: Vladimir Guerrero Sr.
aliases: Vladimir Guerrero Alvino; Vlad the Impaler; Vladdy; Vlad Sr.; Vladimir Guerrero
description: Vladimir Guerrero Sr. is a Dominican former professional baseball right fielder and designated hitter inducted into the National Baseball Hall of Fame in 2018. Born February 9, 1975, in Nizao, Dominican Republic, he was signed by the Montreal Expos at age 18 and debuted on September 19, 1996. With Montreal from 1996 to 2003 he emerged as a power-and-average hitter known for driving pitches outside the strike zone and for a powerful throwing arm. Signing with the Angels as a free agent after 2003, he won the American League Most Valuable Player Award in 2004, his first season with the club. He played for the Angels through 2009, then for the Texas Rangers in 2010 and the Baltimore Orioles in 2011, retiring after that season. Over 16 seasons he recorded a .318 batting average, 449 home runs, 1,496 runs batted in and 2,590 hits, with nine All-Star selections and eight Silver Slugger Awards. He is the father of Toronto Blue Jays star Vladimir Guerrero Jr.
